_help.about: [PARTLY WIRED — the tunnel (queue 100), the surface size (queue 99), the exits for the HUD compass (queue 101); the rest design §FM.8, not wired] The ruin roster and its fixed compass (Mike, 9 Oct). REFERENCE ONLY: only the tomb is built, and Mike said the other ruins go in the reference doc, not the queue. Nothing reads this file yet. The prose and the sources are in docs/design/RUIN_ROSTER_REFERENCE.md; where they differ, the doc wins.
_help.map: reference_only: the map shows where you have been and which way things lie, and takes you nowhere. fast_travel false: for now this supersedes worlds.json → map.fast_travel (§EW) and the map return of §FK.3 (§FM.8).
_help.walk: fixed: the same neighbours every playthrough. Each ruin's inside still comes from the game's seed (§FK.2) and the first ruin is still drawn at random (§FJ.1). Open (§FM.10 call 3): whether walking a direction replaces or sits beside worlds.json → links (the underground passage).
_help.ruins: id: culture, stone (what the ruin is built of), plant (its species and rite, one line, no doses or preparation), plant_status (in_game or not_in_game as of 9 Oct), exits (cardinal direction to the neighbouring ruin id). status: built (the tomb only), reference, or invented (no real ruin; ours). null exits are unplaced. plant_status entry_in_data_sacred_not_drawn: the species entry is in data/sacred/sacred_plants.json (9 Oct, §FM.9) but nothing loads or draws it yet.
_help.egypt: §FO.1, §FP (10 Oct): Egypt is a ruin kind, not a world, and is UNPLACED: Mike has not put it on the compass (null exits, like the taiga), and its biome world is open (§FO.9 call 2). Stone: big sandstone blocks (Mike); true_pyramid in ruins.json is the nearest style, not wired. Plants: blue lotus and mandrake (Mike, 10 Oct, §FP.4), entries in data/sacred/sacred_plants.json, not loaded or drawn. Reference only, like every ruin but the tomb.
_help.maya: §FQ (10 Oct): the Maya are a ruin kind inside a biome world (§FN.0.2), not a world of their own. Limestone temple in jungle, the Maya calendar as its motif, Camazotz as its boss (data/maya_ruin.json). Plant: still open (§FN.8 call 2: Mike gave the mushroom to the Aztec). Biome world: the jungle (§FS.1).
_help.fv: §FV (11 Oct, Mike by voice): the compass walk is a shrine at the surface's edge and a tunnel to the neighbour whose stone changes from this culture's to the next's (answers §FM.10 call 3); surfaces are much smaller (first guess in surface.across_m, Claude's, not Mike's number); the sacred plant grows in sight of the path; nothing gates the way on (tunnels open from the start; §FO.3's boss seal is §FV.7 call 2). plains and tundra are new, placement invented from Mike's 'north from that … the plains … or some type of tundra'; no plant chosen.
_help.tunnel_built: Wired 12 Oct (Claude Code, queue 100, §FV.2, §FV.5; RuinTunnel, Surface, CrawlerMain, CrawlerSave). Mike, 12 Oct: "you can go to the surface and head down another shrine on the cardinal direction of whatever you choose and youll go down that corridor and itll lead to a new biome ruin where you then emerge on the surface and then can go into the new biomes ruins". built_pair (added): which built ruins the tunnel joins, by crawler.json theme and direction. The tomb has no compass row of its own (the aztec row is its stand-in), so the tomb and the Aztec temple are not neighbours on the compass; they are joined anyway along that row's north-south line, Claude Code's choice for Mike to move: the temple's shrine at its surface's south edge, the tomb's at its north edge. A shrine stands only while its neighbour is in the game (the temple: aztec_temple.json enabled). on (added): false lays no shrine. stretch_m (added): each of the three stretches' length; half_m, height_m: the run's half width and height; mix_band_m: the mixed stretch's bands, each wholly one style or the other, the next's the likelier further along; end_m: how near an end you step through; fade_s: the dark each way; log_down, log_up: the log's lines. shrine (added): width_m, depth_m, height_m of the little stone house; in_from_talus_m: how far in from the foot of the edge's slope it stands; in_at_m: how far through its doorway you go down; out_m: where you stand coming up. from, arrive, stretches, gated, boss, reversible and hides_load describe what is built; residents stays open (§FV.7 call 4): none.
_help.earth_home: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FY.10] (22 Oct) Where each ruin kind may spawn on the real Earth (§FX): a culture ruin needs BOTH its region box (lat/lon degrees, generous) AND one of its biomes; a biome ruin needs only its biome. First guesses for Mike's eye. The compass walk above is reference only from 22 Oct.

aztec.plant: Ipomoea corymbosa (ololiuhqui): priests' and healers' divination

peyote_country.stone: adobe and sandstone (Claude's suggestion; real adobe analogue: Paquime)
peyote_country.plant: Lophophora williamsii (peyote): the Wirikuta pilgrimage; IUCN Vulnerable, so the shaman teaches the respectful harvest (Mike)

pueblo.stone: sandstone blocks in mud mortar, cliff alcoves
pueblo.plant: Datura wrightii (sacred datura): Southwest divination and rain rites; a different experience, not a harder one (Mike)

gulf_swamp.culture: Gulf South mound builders (analogues: Poverty Point, Moundville)
gulf_swamp.boss: the witch (§FE.3); her false-shaman sequence is §FR
gulf_swamp.setting: Southeast bayou country (Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida)

maya.stone: limestone (pale; once red-painted stucco, now bare grey) — Mike, 10 Oct
maya.plant: Psilocybe mexicana (teonanacatl): shared with the Aztec rites; Maya use indirect and debated
maya.boss: Camazotz, the death bat (§FQ.2); unplaced in bosses.json
maya.setting: lowland jungle, the Yucatan and Peten heartland; a cenote as the way down (open, §FQ.5 call 3)
maya.biome_world: jungle (Mike, 10 Oct, §FS.1; worlds.json names no jungle world yet)

inca.culture: Inca (San Pedro rites are older, Chavin)
inca.stone: precision-cut andesite and granite, no mortar
inca.plant: Echinopsis pachanoi (San Pedro): northern Peruvian healers' mesa rites; and Erythroxylum coca, a mild chewable offered to the mountain spirits (no effect chosen)

amazon.culture: Amazonian peoples (Acre geoglyphs, Llanos de Mojos mounds)
amazon.plant: Banisteriopsis caapi (the ayahuasca vine): visionary and healing rites

great_zimbabwe.culture: Shona (Great Zimbabwe, about the 11th to 15th century)
great_zimbabwe.plant: Boophone disticha (leshoma): healers' divination and initiation; a poisonous bulb

taiga.stone: none: dark timber, log-and-earth, bone and antler

egypt.stone: big sandstone blocks (Mike); nearest style data/ruins.json true_pyramid
egypt.plant: Nymphaea caerulea (blue lotus) and Mandragora officinarum (mandrake): the Egyptian brew (§FP.4); both thin on evidence, neither native to a hot-desert ruin (§FP.5)

plains.culture: Plains peoples (open: which; Mike named only 'the plains')

tundra.culture: Arctic tundra peoples (open: which); the taiga ruin may belong here or beside it, §FV.7 call 5

tunnel.log_down: Down the shrine's steps, into a long dark way.
tunnel.log_up: Up the shrine's steps, under the open sky.
